shipped_rows.title_o: Figure-Ground Asymmetries in the Implicit Association Test (IAT)

blind_target.evidence_quote: However, the construct validity of this type of IAT has been called into question by recent findings showing that the IAT score implying in-group preference is rather driven by the salience asymmetry within each categorical dyad of the procedure than by evaluative associations between concepts (Rothermund & Wentura, 2001, 2004).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Consistent with our predictions, results showed that in both cases salience asymmetries reliably predict the IAT effect.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract identifies both earlier salience-asymmetry findings and reports the corresponding predicted relationship in both new experiments. Bibliographic titles and original study numbers are absent from the abstract.
